Run focused source tests, inspect actual assertions and implementation, report concrete severity/file/line/reproduction evidence; distinguish baseline failures. Include pi naming/import/path remnants in a separate section. Do not edit product files, build daily-driver dist, access credentials, install, publish, use live providers/services or modify GitHub. Acceptance level: reviewed
Completion is not accepted from prose alone. End with a structured acceptance report.

Criteria:
- criterion-1: Implement the requested change without widening scope
- criterion-2: Return evidence sufficient for an independent acceptance review

Required evidence: changed-files, tests-added, commands-run, validation-output, residual-risks, no-staged-files

Use empty arrays when no items apply; array fields contain strings unless object entries are shown.
`criteriaSatisfied[].status` must be exactly one of: satisfied, not-satisfied, not-applicable.
`commandsRun[].result` must be exactly one of: passed, failed, not-run.
`manualNotes` and `notes` are optional strings; an empty string means no note and does not satisfy `manual-notes` evidence.

    {
      "id": "criterion-1",
      "status": "satisfied",

}
```

50:{"n":65,"title":"perf: cut first-request startup latency by half","merged":true,"body":"PR #50 cut first-request startup latency, but its lazy lifecycle handling and public package checks had regressions. That merge was reverted. This replacement keeps the startup improvement and repairs the failure paths found in the follow-up review.

- Keep web, LSP, MCP, and subagent implementations lazy while registering their tools and required hooks before the first request.
- Isolate web request and curator state per extension factory. Close partial or in-flight MCP work, serialize LSP shutdown, and wait for subagent launch registration without serializing foreground children.
- Emit gateway and cron `session_shutdown` before disposal, including reset, resume, switching, and eviction paths.
- Restore the public RPC entry through a bundle-first wrapper. Validate wildcard exports and recursively scan staged compiled files before publishing.
- Keep PR #41 terminal sanitization out of this branch.

## Measurements

Windows, Node 24.15.0, local provider, ten samples per cell. Baseline `b709d12` has instrumentation only. No remote model or reboot-cold filesystem measurement.

| First request | Before median / p95 | After median / p95 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fresh profile | 1988.8 / 2026.4 ms | 968.2 / 1007.0 ms |
| Repeated launch | 2597.6 / 2628.6 ms | 970.6 / 993.5 ms |

Median improvement is 51.3% fresh and 62.6% repeated. The complete default tool payload remains identical. These are controlled measurements, not a latency guarantee. First-use MCP status varied from about 126 ms to 3.1 seconds. Details and reproduction commands are in `packages/coding-agent/docs/interactive-startup.md`.

## Verification

- Offline builds pass for TUI, AI, agent, coding-agent, and orchestrator.
- Focused lifecycle and package tests pass 89/89.
- The built-CLI checker passes stalled and failed runtime cases, blocked optional imports, and real first-turn subagent, MCP, LSP, and fetch calls.
- All four public-package dry-run packs pass. Relative imports, shrinkwrap, installer lock, workflow policy, browser smoke, and diff checks pass.
- Full coding-agent Vitest matches the current baseline at 2431 passed, 112 unrelated Windows and stale-fixture failures, and 47 skipped. TUI retains four Windows symlink failures. Repository Biome retains 20 existing findings.

No release, catalog regeneration, installed-CLI change, or PR #41 terminal change is included.

PR filed and repaired by GPT-5.6 sol in the lunR agent.
"}
53:{"n":62,"title":"fix: keep subagent description in the tool schema","merged":true,"body":"Grok could not launch children. Every child needs a short UI label called `description`, but a schema cleanup deleted that field because JSON Schema also uses `description` for help text. The model was not allowed to send the label, then lunR rejected the launch.

Grok also fills every optional field on the flat tool, so a real launch arrived with `action: \"status\"` and dummy `tasks`/`chain`. Once validation passed, that would have become a status call instead of a spawn.

The cleanup now keeps `description` when it is a real parameter and still strips nested help text. A control `action` mixed into a launch is dropped, except `schedule` / `append-step` / `resume` / `steer`. Tests cover the pruned schema Grok actually sees and that mixed payload.

Supersedes #61.

PR filed by grok-4.6 xhigh in lunR agent."}

Todos and the async widget were stacked with no gap, the running glyph was frozen on a seed, and async chrome did not match compact foreground rows. There is now a blank row and a dim rule between those widgets. A running async child uses the same description-first compact row (`modelSelection` badge, hang line of tools · tokens · time). 65:{"n":50,"title":"perf: cut first-request startup latency by half","merged":true,"body":"The chatbox appeared early, but the first request still waited for unused implementation modules. This keeps the required startup hooks and tool schemas, while reducing the code Node loads before dispatch.

- Share split Node bundles between the CLI and SDK. Load web, LSP, MCP, and subagent engines on demand.
- Cancel stale initialization and prevent old web results, curator callbacks, MCP connections, and LSP diagnostics from entering a replacement session.
- Check the built CLI with optional imports blocked, then exercise real first-turn tools. Verify public-name tarball installation and SDK class identity.

## Measurements

Windows, Node 24.15.0, local provider, ten samples per cell. Baseline `b709d12` has instrumentation only. No remote model or reboot-cold filesystem measurement.

| First request | Before median / p95 | After median / p95 |
| --- | --- | --- |

| Repeated launch | 2597.6 / 2628.6 ms | 970.6 / 993.5 ms |

Median improvement is 51.3% fresh and 62.6% repeated. The complete default tool payload remains identical. These are controlled measurements, not a latency guarantee. First-use MCP status varied from about 126 ms to 3.1 seconds. Details and reproduction commands are in `packages/coding-agent/docs/interactive-startup.md`.

## Verification

- Rebased onto current master at v0.2.16. Five-package offline build passes without catalog regeneration.
- Node 22.19 and 24 built-CLI checks pass. Public tarballs with shrinkwrap install successfully; JS/TS extension SDK identity, SDK session creation, and RPC checks pass.
- Full coding-agent suite: 2405 passed, 112 failed, 47 skipped. The failed test names match the baseline exactly. AI compat/lazy/Faux tests: 28 passed.
- Touched-file Biome and dependency/import/lock/workflow/browser checks pass. Repository-wide Biome retains existing failures.
- Bun 1.4.2 source launch completes a local request. Standalone compilation fails on both baseline and branch because the isolated ignore-scripts install lacks the native canvas binary.

68:{"n":47,"title":"release: ship lunR 0.2.15","merged":true,"body":"Stable lunR was missing the two `/settings` rows that already exist on lunr-dev: Model instructions and Confirm large subagent launches.

74:{"n":41,"title":"perf: accept terminal input in 130ms and harden runtime safety","merged":false,"body":"Typing `lunr` still made the terminal wait for the whole runtime before it accepted input. The same audit found several concrete safety and scaling bugs in permissions, rollback, orchestration, terminal input, pinned chat, and release builds.

A fresh isolated benchmark now arms input at 127 ms and commits the first frame at 131 ms. Runtime hydration finished at 2.53 s and the complete prompt barrier opened at 3.87 s in that run.

The reliability pass also:

- rejects rollback symlink escapes and corrupt session graphs
- bounds RPC and Radius cleanup, and writes orchestrator state atomically
- strips unsafe terminal controls and fixes Unicode and narrow-viewport input cases
- preserves pinned-chat caches for paint-only footer updates without serving stale chat
- removes synchronous footer git work and duplicate model refresh work
- makes CI, binary builds, and local public-package staging deterministic and offline
- records the audit and launch design in two root review documents

- offline TUI, AI, agent, coding-agent, and orchestrator TypeScript builds passed
- focused TUI tests passed, 98 tests

- focused orchestrator tests passed, 7 tests

- local release staging and full package build passed in the isolated worker

Still deferred: the manual npm dispatch source-tag guard, deeper settings and resource indexing, lazy auth initialization, deferred-tool retry controls, lifecycle cancellation, and PTY/ConPTY benchmark coverage.

88:{"n":27,"title":"docs: lunR identity for the published npm package","merged":true,"body":"## Summary

90:{"n":25,"title":"fix: eliminate disabled-watchdog cold-start scans","merged":true,"body":"## Summary

- remove eager Git worktree fingerprinting from watchdog construction and session binding
- gate repository signatures on the effective main-watchdog enablement state
- lazily establish the repo-edit baseline at the first relevant `before_agent_start`
- clear signature state across session and disable boundaries
- add regression coverage for disabled startup, enabled change review, pre-existing dirty files, and session rebinding

## Root cause

`MainWatchdogRuntime` computed the complete repository change signature in its constructor, then twice more while binding the initial session. This happened even though the main watchdog is disabled by default. The signature invokes Git status and stats/hashes dirty paths, so Windows cold filesystem, Defender, and OneDrive state could turn deferred subagent attachment into a multi-second first-prompt delay.

The fix removes all constructor/session-bind scans. An enabled repo-edit watchdog now fingerprints once at turn start and once at agent end, preserving the existing rule that only edits made during that turn trigger review.

## Verification

- focused Vitest regression set: 25/25 passed
- required tsgo build sequence passed: tui, ai, agent, coding-agent, orchestrator
- touched-file Biome passed; the vendored watchdog source remains excluded by repository configuration
- dirty-worktree startup benchmark: prompt-ready 2.23s, deferred attach 265ms, `pi-subagents` factory 6ms

The full coding-agent suite was also attempted: 2236 tests passed and 125 failed in unrelated current-master/Windows areas; no watchdog test failed. Full Biome reports 35 existing errors and one warning outside the touched files.

## Out of scope

The larger first-paint ESM/TypeBox module graph remains a secondary cold-cache amplifier. This PR intentionally does not refactor that graph or the startup profiler; it fixes only the experimentally isolated default-off watchdog scan.
"}

113:{"n":2,"title":"feat(agent): agent-swarm approval gate for auto-activated parallel fan-out","merged":false,"body":"## What

An auto-activated agent swarm — one `subagent` tool call launching **more than 2 parallel subagents** — now requires user approval in **manual and yolo** modes. Only `auto` mode bypasses the gate. Explicit `/swarm` turns are pre-approved (the user already asked for the swarm).

TUI dialog:

```
▶ Approve AgentSwarm?

agent swarm (4 subagents)
Explore lunR auth/model/settings/plan systems

  1. Approve once
  2. Approve for this session
  3. Reject
  4. Reject with feedback
```

Reject-with-feedback collects a one-line reason that becomes the block reason the model sees, so it can adjust the plan. On approval the footer shows `swarm ● active` for the rest of the turn, same as an explicit /swarm.

## How

- `core/swarm.ts`: `SWARM_APPROVAL_THRESHOLD` (2), `effectiveSwarmCount` (tasks[] with `count` multipliers + chain `parallel` blocks; dynamic `expand` fan-out has no static count and is not gated), `isExplicitSwarmTurn` (last user message starts with `[SWARM MODE]` — works for TUI + gateway since both inject the same prompt).
- `core/permissions.ts`: swarm branch in `gateToolCall` runs before the mode early-return so yolo is gated too; `ApprovalResponse` is now decision strings OR `{ decision: "reject", feedback }`; `ApprovalRequest.kind?: "swarm"`; session approval under the `"swarm"` action key; fail-closed without a handler.
- `agent-session.ts`: computes `explicitSwarmTurn` from the branch, passes via new `GateOptions`.
- TUI: `showSwarmApprovalDialog`; `ExtensionSelectorComponent` gains 1-9 number-key selection (all selectors).
- Gateway: AgentSwarm prompt title; buttons stay once/session/reject — inline buttons can't capture free text, so reject-with-feedback is TUI-only.

## Verification

- `permissions.test.ts` grew to 26 tests (swarm count helpers, mode matrix, explicit-swarm exemption, session approval, reject-feedback reason, fail-closed) — all pass
- `gateway-approval.test.ts` (6) passes
- Build agent → coding-agent → orchestrator all exit 0; `biome check packages/` clean; `npx lunr --print` smoke responds

Interactive dialog flow not live-tested in this environment.
"}

50:{"n":65,"title":"perf: cut first-request startup latency by half","merged":true,"body":"PR #50 cut first-request startup latency, but its lazy lifecycle handling and public package checks had regressions. That merge was reverted. This replacement keeps the startup improvement and repairs the failure paths found in the follow-up review.

- Keep web, LSP, MCP, and subagent implementations lazy while registering their tools and required hooks before the first request.
- Isolate web request and curator state per extension factory. Close partial or in-flight MCP work, serialize LSP shutdown, and wait for subagent launch registration without serializing foreground children.
- Emit gateway and cron `session_shutdown` before disposal, including reset, resume, switching, and eviction paths.
- Restore the public RPC entry through a bundle-first wrapper. Validate wildcard exports and recursively scan staged compiled files before publishing.
- Keep PR #41 terminal sanitization out of this branch.

## Measurements

Windows, Node 24.15.0, local provider, ten samples per cell. Baseline `b709d12` has instrumentation only. No remote model or reboot-cold filesystem measurement.

| First request | Before median / p95 | After median / p95 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fresh profile | 1988.8 / 2026.4 ms | 968.2 / 1007.0 ms |
| Repeated launch | 2597.6 / 2628.6 ms | 970.6 / 993.5 ms |

Median improvement is 51.3% fresh and 62.6% repeated. The complete default tool payload remains identical. These are controlled measurements, not a latency guarantee. First-use MCP status varied from about 126 ms to 3.1 seconds. Details and reproduction commands are in `packages/coding-agent/docs/interactive-startup.md`.

## Verification

- Offline builds pass for TUI, AI, agent, coding-agent, and orchestrator.
- Focused lifecycle and package tests pass 89/89.
- The built-CLI checker passes stalled and failed runtime cases, blocked optional imports, and real first-turn subagent, MCP, LSP, and fetch calls.
- All four public-package dry-run packs pass. Relative imports, shrinkwrap, installer lock, workflow policy, browser smoke, and diff checks pass.
- Full coding-agent Vitest matches the current baseline at 2431 passed, 112 unrelated Windows and stale-fixture failures, and 47 skipped. TUI retains four Windows symlink failures. Repository Biome retains 20 existing findings.

No release, catalog regeneration, installed-CLI change, or PR #41 terminal change is included.

PR filed and repaired by GPT-5.6 sol in the lunR agent.
"}
53:{"n":62,"title":"fix: keep subagent description in the tool schema","merged":true,"body":"Grok could not launch children. Every child needs a short UI label called `description`, but a schema cleanup deleted that field because JSON Schema also uses `description` for help text. The model was not allowed to send the label, then lunR rejected the launch.

Grok also fills every optional field on the flat tool, so a real launch arrived with `action: \"status\"` and dummy `tasks`/`chain`. Once validation passed, that would have become a status call instead of a spawn.

The cleanup now keeps `description` when it is a real parameter and still strips nested help text. A control `action` mixed into a launch is dropped, except `schedule` / `append-step` / `resume` / `steer`. Tests cover the pruned schema Grok actually sees and that mixed payload.

Supersedes #61.

PR filed by grok-4.6 xhigh in lunR agent."}

65:{"n":50,"title":"perf: cut first-request startup latency by half","merged":true,"body":"The chatbox appeared early, but the first request still waited for unused implementation modules. This keeps the required startup hooks and tool schemas, while reducing the code Node loads before dispatch.

- Share split Node bundles between the CLI and SDK. Load web, LSP, MCP, and subagent engines on demand.

- Check the built CLI with optional imports blocked, then exercise real first-turn tools. Verify public-name tarball installation and SDK class identity.

## Measurements

Windows, Node 24.15.0, local provider, ten samples per cell. Baseline `b709d12` has instrumentation only. No remote model or reboot-cold filesystem measurement.

| First request | Before median / p95 | After median / p95 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fresh profile | 1988.8 / 2026.4 ms | 968.2 / 1007.0 ms |
| Repeated launch | 2597.6 / 2628.6 ms | 970.6 / 993.5 ms |

Median improvement is 51.3% fresh and 62.6% repeated. The complete default tool payload remains identical. These are controlled measurements, not a latency guarantee. First-use MCP status varied from about 126 ms to 3.1 seconds. Details and reproduction commands are in `packages/coding-agent/docs/interactive-startup.md`.

## Verification

- Rebased onto current master at v0.2.16. Five-package offline build passes without catalog regeneration.
- Node 22.19 and 24 built-CLI checks pass. Public tarballs with shrinkwrap install successfully; JS/TS extension SDK identity, SDK session creation, and RPC checks pass.
- Full coding-agent suite: 2405 passed, 112 failed, 47 skipped. The failed test names match the baseline exactly. AI compat/lazy/Faux tests: 28 passed.
- Touched-file Biome and dependency/import/lock/workflow/browser checks pass. Repository-wide Biome retains existing failures.
- Bun 1.4.2 source launch completes a local request. Standalone compilation fails on both baseline and branch because the isolated ignore-scripts install lacks the native canvas binary.

74:{"n":41,"title":"perf: accept terminal input in 130ms and harden runtime safety","merged":false,"body":"Typing `lunr` still made the terminal wait for the whole runtime before it accepted input. The same audit found several concrete safety and scaling bugs in permissions, rollback, orchestration, terminal input, pinned chat, and release builds.

This changes interactive startup to paint a small editor shell first, then hydrate models, resources, sessions, and extensions behind the prompt barrier. A fresh isolated benchmark now arms input at 127 ms and commits the first frame at 131 ms. Runtime hydration finished at 2.53 s and the complete prompt barrier opened at 3.87 s in that run.

The reliability pass also:

- requires Manual approval for full-access child launches
- rejects rollback symlink escapes and corrupt session graphs
- bounds RPC and Radius cleanup, and writes orchestrator state atomically
- strips unsafe terminal controls and fixes Unicode and narrow-viewport input cases
- preserves pinned-chat caches for paint-only footer updates without serving stale chat
- removes synchronous footer git work and duplicate model refresh work
- makes CI, binary builds, and local public-package staging deterministic and offline
- records the audit and launch design in two root review documents

Validation:

- offline TUI, AI, agent, coding-agent, and orchestrator TypeScript builds passed
- focused TUI tests passed, 98 tests
- focused coding-agent tests passed, 134 tests
- focused orchestrator tests passed, 7 tests
- changed-code Biome and `git diff --check` passed
- isolated startup benchmark passed with input armed at 127 ms
- rebuilt `npx lunr --version` returned 0.2.13
- rebuilt print-mode smoke returned `smoke-ok` before the known print-mode process timeout
- local release staging and full package build passed in the isolated worker

Still deferred: the manual npm dispatch source-tag guard, deeper settings and resource indexing, lazy auth initialization, deferred-tool retry controls, lifecycle cancellation, and PTY/ConPTY benchmark coverage.

PR filed by GPT 5.6 sol in the lunR agent.
"}

90:{"n":25,"title":"fix: eliminate disabled-watchdog cold-start scans","merged":true,"body":"## Summary

- remove eager Git worktree fingerprinting from watchdog construction and session binding
- gate repository signatures on the effective main-watchdog enablement state
- lazily establish the repo-edit baseline at the first relevant `before_agent_start`
- clear signature state across session and disable boundaries
- add regression coverage for disabled startup, enabled change review, pre-existing dirty files, and session rebinding

## Root cause

`MainWatchdogRuntime` computed the complete repository change signature in its constructor, then twice more while binding the initial session. This happened even though the main watchdog is disabled by default. The signature invokes Git status and stats/hashes dirty paths, so Windows cold filesystem, Defender, and OneDrive state could turn deferred subagent attachment into a multi-second first-prompt delay.

The fix removes all constructor/session-bind scans. An enabled repo-edit watchdog now fingerprints once at turn start and once at agent end, preserving the existing rule that only edits made during that turn trigger review.

## Verification

- focused Vitest regression set: 25/25 passed
- required tsgo build sequence passed: tui, ai, agent, coding-agent, orchestrator
- touched-file Biome passed; the vendored watchdog source remains excluded by repository configuration
- dirty-worktree startup benchmark: prompt-ready 2.23s, deferred attach 265ms, `pi-subagents` factory 6ms

The full coding-agent suite was also attempted: 2236 tests passed and 125 failed in unrelated current-master/Windows areas; no watchdog test failed. Full Biome reports 35 existing errors and one warning outside the touched files.

## Out of scope

The larger first-paint ESM/TypeBox module graph remains a secondary cold-cache amplifier. This PR intentionally does not refactor that graph or the startup profiler; it fixes only the experimentally isolated default-off watchdog scan.

113:{"n":2,"title":"feat(agent): agent-swarm approval gate for auto-activated parallel fan-out","merged":false,"body":"## What

An auto-activated agent swarm — one `subagent` tool call launching **more than 2 parallel subagents** — now requires user approval in **manual and yolo** modes. Only `auto` mode bypasses the gate. Explicit `/swarm` turns are pre-approved (the user already asked for the swarm).

TUI dialog:

```
▶ Approve AgentSwarm?

agent swarm (4 subagents)
Explore lunR auth/model/settings/plan systems

  1. Approve once
  2. Approve for this session
  3. Reject
  4. Reject with feedback
```

Reject-with-feedback collects a one-line reason that becomes the block reason the model sees, so it can adjust the plan. On approval the footer shows `swarm ● active` for the rest of the turn, same as an explicit /swarm.

## How

- `core/swarm.ts`: `SWARM_APPROVAL_THRESHOLD` (2), `effectiveSwarmCount` (tasks[] with `count` multipliers + chain `parallel` blocks; dynamic `expand` fan-out has no static count and is not gated), `isExplicitSwarmTurn` (last user message starts with `[SWARM MODE]` — works for TUI + gateway since both inject the same prompt).
- `core/permissions.ts`: swarm branch in `gateToolCall` runs before the mode early-return so yolo is gated too; `ApprovalResponse` is now decision strings OR `{ decision: "reject", feedback }`; `ApprovalRequest.kind?: "swarm"`; session approval under the `"swarm"` action key; fail-closed without a handler.
- `agent-session.ts`: computes `explicitSwarmTurn` from the branch, passes via new `GateOptions`.
- TUI: `showSwarmApprovalDialog`; `ExtensionSelectorComponent` gains 1-9 number-key selection (all selectors).
- Gateway: AgentSwarm prompt title; buttons stay once/session/reject — inline buttons can't capture free text, so reject-with-feedback is TUI-only.

## Verification

- `permissions.test.ts` grew to 26 tests (swarm count helpers, mode matrix, explicit-swarm exemption, session approval, reject-feedback reason, fail-closed) — all pass
- `gateway-approval.test.ts` (6) passes
- Build agent → coding-agent → orchestrator all exit 0; `biome check packages/` clean; `npx lunr --print` smoke responds

Interactive dialog flow not live-tested in this environment.
"}

50:{"n":65,"title":"perf: cut first-request startup latency by half","merged":true,"body":"PR #50 cut first-request startup latency, but its lazy lifecycle handling and public package checks had regressions. That merge was reverted. This replacement keeps the startup improvement and repairs the failure paths found in the follow-up review.

- Keep web, LSP, MCP, and subagent implementations lazy while registering their tools and required hooks before the first request.
- Isolate web request and curator state per extension factory. Close partial or in-flight MCP work, serialize LSP shutdown, and wait for subagent launch registration without serializing foreground children.
- Emit gateway and cron `session_shutdown` before disposal, including reset, resume, switching, and eviction paths.
- Restore the public RPC entry through a bundle-first wrapper. Validate wildcard exports and recursively scan staged compiled files before publishing.
- Keep PR #41 terminal sanitization out of this branch.

## Measurements

Windows, Node 24.15.0, local provider, ten samples per cell. Baseline `b709d12` has instrumentation only. No remote model or reboot-cold filesystem measurement.

| First request | Before median / p95 | After median / p95 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fresh profile | 1988.8 / 2026.4 ms | 968.2 / 1007.0 ms |
| Repeated launch | 2597.6 / 2628.6 ms | 970.6 / 993.5 ms |

Median improvement is 51.3% fresh and 62.6% repeated. The complete default tool payload remains identical. These are controlled measurements, not a latency guarantee. First-use MCP status varied from about 126 ms to 3.1 seconds. Details and reproduction commands are in `packages/coding-agent/docs/interactive-startup.md`.

## Verification

- Offline builds pass for TUI, AI, agent, coding-agent, and orchestrator.
- Focused lifecycle and package tests pass 89/89.
- The built-CLI checker passes stalled and failed runtime cases, blocked optional imports, and real first-turn subagent, MCP, LSP, and fetch calls.
- All four public-package dry-run packs pass. Relative imports, shrinkwrap, installer lock, workflow policy, browser smoke, and diff checks pass.
- Full coding-agent Vitest matches the current baseline at 2431 passed, 112 unrelated Windows and stale-fixture failures, and 47 skipped. TUI retains four Windows symlink failures. Repository Biome retains 20 existing findings.

No release, catalog regeneration, installed-CLI change, or PR #41 terminal change is included.

PR filed and repaired by GPT-5.6 sol in the lunR agent.
"}
53:{"n":62,"title":"fix: keep subagent description in the tool schema","merged":true,"body":"Grok could not launch children. Every child needs a short UI label called `description`, but a schema cleanup deleted that field because JSON Schema also uses `description` for help text. The model was not allowed to send the label, then lunR rejected the launch.

Grok also fills every optional field on the flat tool, so a real launch arrived with `action: \"status\"` and dummy `tasks`/`chain`. Once validation passed, that would have become a status call instead of a spawn.

The cleanup now keeps `description` when it is a real parameter and still strips nested help text. A control `action` mixed into a launch is dropped, except `schedule` / `append-step` / `resume` / `steer`. Tests cover the pruned schema Grok actually sees and that mixed payload.

Supersedes #61.

PR filed by grok-4.6 xhigh in lunR agent."}

90:{"n":25,"title":"fix: eliminate disabled-watchdog cold-start scans","merged":true,"body":"## Summary

- remove eager Git worktree fingerprinting from watchdog construction and session binding
- gate repository signatures on the effective main-watchdog enablement state
- lazily establish the repo-edit baseline at the first relevant `before_agent_start`
- clear signature state across session and disable boundaries
- add regression coverage for disabled startup, enabled change review, pre-existing dirty files, and session rebinding

## Root cause

`MainWatchdogRuntime` computed the complete repository change signature in its constructor, then twice more while binding the initial session. This happened even though the main watchdog is disabled by default. The signature invokes Git status and stats/hashes dirty paths, so Windows cold filesystem, Defender, and OneDrive state could turn deferred subagent attachment into a multi-second first-prompt delay.

The fix removes all constructor/session-bind scans. An enabled repo-edit watchdog now fingerprints once at turn start and once at agent end, preserving the existing rule that only edits made during that turn trigger review.

## Verification

- focused Vitest regression set: 25/25 passed
- required tsgo build sequence passed: tui, ai, agent, coding-agent, orchestrator
- touched-file Biome passed; the vendored watchdog source remains excluded by repository configuration
- dirty-worktree startup benchmark: prompt-ready 2.23s, deferred attach 265ms, `pi-subagents` factory 6ms

The full coding-agent suite was also attempted: 2236 tests passed and 125 failed in unrelated current-master/Windows areas; no watchdog test failed. Full Biome reports 35 existing errors and one warning outside the touched files.

## Out of scope

The larger first-paint ESM/TypeBox module graph remains a secondary cold-cache amplifier. This PR intentionally does not refactor that graph or the startup profiler; it fixes only the experimentally isolated default-off watchdog scan.

113:{"n":2,"title":"feat(agent): agent-swarm approval gate for auto-activated parallel fan-out","merged":false,"body":"## What

An auto-activated agent swarm — one `subagent` tool call launching **more than 2 parallel subagents** — now requires user approval in **manual and yolo** modes. Only `auto` mode bypasses the gate. Explicit `/swarm` turns are pre-approved (the user already asked for the swarm).

TUI dialog:

```
▶ Approve AgentSwarm?

agent swarm (4 subagents)
Explore lunR auth/model/settings/plan systems

  1. Approve once
  2. Approve for this session
  3. Reject
  4. Reject with feedback
```

Reject-with-feedback collects a one-line reason that becomes the block reason the model sees, so it can adjust the plan. On approval the footer shows `swarm ● active` for the rest of the turn, same as an explicit /swarm.

## How

- `core/swarm.ts`: `SWARM_APPROVAL_THRESHOLD` (2), `effectiveSwarmCount` (tasks[] with `count` multipliers + chain `parallel` blocks; dynamic `expand` fan-out has no static count and is not gated), `isExplicitSwarmTurn` (last user message starts with `[SWARM MODE]` — works for TUI + gateway since both inject the same prompt).
- `core/permissions.ts`: swarm branch in `gateToolCall` runs before the mode early-return so yolo is gated too; `ApprovalResponse` is now decision strings OR `{ decision: "reject", feedback }`; `ApprovalRequest.kind?: "swarm"`; session approval under the `"swarm"` action key; fail-closed without a handler.
- `agent-session.ts`: computes `explicitSwarmTurn` from the branch, passes via new `GateOptions`.
- TUI: `showSwarmApprovalDialog`; `ExtensionSelectorComponent` gains 1-9 number-key selection (all selectors).
- Gateway: AgentSwarm prompt title; buttons stay once/session/reject — inline buttons can't capture free text, so reject-with-feedback is TUI-only.

## Verification

- `permissions.test.ts` grew to 26 tests (swarm count helpers, mode matrix, explicit-swarm exemption, session approval, reject-feedback reason, fail-closed) — all pass
- `gateway-approval.test.ts` (6) passes
- Build agent → coding-agent → orchestrator all exit 0; `biome check packages/` clean; `npx lunr --print` smoke responds

Interactive dialog flow not live-tested in this environment.
"}

/**
 * lunr: read-only tool-gating heuristics + system-prompt addendum.
 *
 * `gateToolCall` in permissions.ts applies `readOnlyModeBlockReason` in read-only mode:
 * `edit`/`write` and mutating `bash` are hard-blocked; read tools stay open.
 * InteractiveMode installs `READ_ONLY_MODE_ADDENDUM` via the shared system-prompt
 * append slot (same slot auto mode uses).
 *
 * Bash heuristic (conservative, blocklist-based — NOT a security boundary):
 * - any `>`/`>>` redirect outside quotes blocks the whole command;
 * - the command is split on `;`, `|`, `&` separators (outside quotes) and every segment's
 *   leading command must be read-only:
 *   - known mutating commands (rm, mv, cp, mkdir, sed -i, tee, …) are blocked;
 *   - `git` is limited to read-only subcommands (status/log/diff/show/… plus flag-only
 *     branch/tag/remote); mutating subcommands (add/commit/push/checkout/…) are blocked;
 *   - package managers are limited to read-only subcommands (install/add/remove/… blocked);
 *   - arbitrary runners (sudo, xargs, npx, sh -c …) are blocked.
 * Unknown-but-not-listed commands are ALLOWED (blocklist, not allowlist) — the model is
 * additionally steered by the system-prompt addendum. False positives are expected; the
 * user can run the command themselves or switch to another mode.
 */

/** Appended to the system prompt while read-only mode is active. */
export const READ_ONLY_MODE_ADDENDUM =
	"You are in read-only mode. Investigate and answer without making changes. If the user asks for a plan, you may call present_plan for approval. Do not implement until the user switches modes or approves that plan.";

export const READ_ONLY_MODE_BLOCK_MESSAGE = "Read-only mode is active; no changes allowed.";

const BLOCKED_TOOLS = new Set(["edit", "write", "memory_add", "memory_remove", "cron"]);

/** Small allowlist of read-only commands permitted in read-only mode. Everything else is rejected. */
const ALLOWED_COMMANDS = new Set([
	"ls",
	"ll",
	"cat",
	"tac",
	"grep",
	"rg",
	"find",
	"pwd",
	"echo",
	"printf",
	"head",
	"tail",
	"wc",
	"less",
	"more",
	"sort",
	"uniq",
	"diff",
	"cmp",
	"comm",
	"test",
	"[",
	"true",
	"false",
	"which",
	"whereis",
	"stat",
	"file",
	"id",
	"whoami",
	"who",
	"date",
	"cal",
	"env",
	"printenv",
	"uname",
	"hostname",
	"uptime",
	"nproc",
	"tput",
	"git",
	"gh",
	"node",
	"npm",
	"pnpm",
	"yarn",
	"bun",
]);

const MUTATING_GIT_SUBCOMMANDS = new Set([
	"add",
	"commit",
	"push",
	"pull",
	"merge",
	"rebase",
	"reset",
	"checkout",
	"switch",
	"restore",
	"rm",
	"mv",
	"stash",
	"cherry-pick",
	"revert",
	"clean",
	"fetch",
	"config",
	"apply",
	"am",
	"init",
	"clone",
	"submodule",
	"worktree",
	"gc",
	"prune",
	"update-index",
]);

// git subcommands that are read-only only when they carry no positional args or
// mutating flags (`git branch` lists, `git branch foo` / `git branch -d foo` mutate).
const CONDITIONAL_GIT_SUBCOMMANDS = new Set(["branch", "tag", "remote"]);
const CONDITIONAL_GIT_MUTATING_FLAGS = new Set(["-d", "-D", "-m", "-M", "-c", "-C"]);

const PACKAGE_MANAGER_MUTATIONS: Record<string, Set<string>> = {
	npm: new Set([
		"install",
		"add",
		"remove",
		"uninstall",
		"update",
		"upgrade",
		"publish",
		"link",
		"unlink",
		"ci",
		"init",
	]),
	pnpm: new Set(["install", "add", "remove", "uninstall", "update", "upgrade", "publish", "link", "unlink", "init"]),
	yarn: new Set(["install", "add", "remove", "uninstall", "upgrade", "publish", "link", "unlink", "init"]),
	bun: new Set(["install", "add", "remove", "uninstall", "update", "upgrade", "publish", "link", "unlink", "init"]),
};

// Almost every subcommand mutates the system.
const ALWAYS_MUTATING_MANAGERS = new Set([
	"apt",
	"apt-get",
	"brew",
	"dnf",
	"yum",
	"pacman",
	"choco",
	"winget",
	"scoop",
]);

/** Flags that cause an interpreter to execute code and are never allowed in read-only mode. */
const EXECUTING_NODE_FLAGS = new Set([
	"-e",
	"--eval",
	"-p",
	"--print",
	"-r",
	"--require",
	"--import",
	"-i",
	"--interactive",
]);

#112 release: integrate current PRs for v0.2.24 M Integrates #106, #107, #109, #110, and #111 with merge ancestry. Resolves overlapping AGENTS.md entries and the permission-mode fixture/test conflicts; refreshes the combined tool-schema snapshot. Does not include #77 or #108. Offline package builds and focused checks pass; five existing Windows .pi settings fixture failures remain. Live Anthropic subscription qualification was not performed.

#104 release: v0.2.23 M Release 0.2.23 with PRs #99 through #103. PR #77 remains open and is excluded. Validation: five offline package builds, coding-agent Node bundle, 249 focused tests plus 17 documented Windows fixture failures, first-paint and first-turn checks, release artifact checks, touched-file Biome, and four-package npm dry-run.

#97 release: v0.2.22 M Prepares v0.2.22 after merging approved PRs #88 and #91 through #96. PR #77 remains open and is excluded. Updates lockstep package versions, changelogs, shrinkwrap, and installer locks.

#86 release: prepare v0.2.21 M Ship the four merged post-0.2.20 PRs as npm 0.2.21. Subagents now launch async unless the parent asks for foreground. Mixed child rows stay compact, Windows intercom starts without the stderr lock, and question/result delivery no longer reports false failures. Native computer use #77 stays open. Package versions, shrinkwrap, and installer locks are 0.2.21. Publication follows the master merge through the existing `v0.2.21` tag workflo

#72 fix: resume async children without discarding their session M Resuming a finished or failed async child rejected the recovery descriptor the runtime had just written. `explicit` and `inferredReason` were treated as illegal launch fields, and persisted `reviewed` was treated as a new explicit reviewer request. Children also could not reach the parent: supervisor/intercom died with `Broker failed to start within timeout` because spawn always launched missing `tsx` plus `broker.ts` from compiled inst

#66 release: ship lunR 0.2.18 M npm is still 0.2.17. Master already has the faster first request, thinking-level slash commands, quieter TUI, injected context card, and compact async subagent rows. 0.2.18 versions the packages and changelog so tagging `v0.2.18` can publish `@ashx-j/lunr`. Validation: - offline builds: tui, ai, agent, coding-agent, orchestrator - focused coding-agent tests: 172 passed - first-paint checker: stalled/failing runtime plus first-turn sub

#62 fix: keep subagent description in the tool schema M Grok could not launch children. Every child needs a short UI label called `description`, but a schema cleanup deleted that field because JSON Schema also uses `description` for help text. The model was not allowed to send the label, then lunR rejected the launch. Grok also fills every optional field on the flat tool, so a real launch arrived with `action: \"status\"` and dummy `tasks`/`chain`. Once validation passed, that would have be

#61 fix: keep subagent description in the tool schema U Grok could not launch subagents. Every child needs a short UI label called `description`, but a schema cleanup deleted that field because JSON Schema also uses `description` for help text. The model was not allowed to send the label, then lunR rejected the launch for missing it. The cleanup now keeps `description` when it is a real parameter and still strips nested help text. Tests cover the pruned schema Grok actually sees. PR filed 

#51 merge: put live 0.2.16 and PR #50 on the lunr-dev channel M The live CLI is 0.2.16 and https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/50 cuts first-request time roughly in half, but `lunr-dev` is still on the older TUI channel. This merge brings both onto `dev/tui` so the next lunr-dev publish has current public lunR plus the lazy web, LSP, MCP, and subagent engines. Keeps the isolated `lunr-dev` binary and npm channel. Keeps first-paint from 0.2.14 instead of #41's temporary shell. Leaves `/swarm` remove

#47 release: ship lunR 0.2.15 M Stable lunR was missing the two `/settings` rows that already exist on lunr-dev: Model instructions and Confirm large subagent launches. This ports that work onto current master (real first paint stays) and bumps to 0.2.15. - Model instructions load `~/.lunr/agent/agents/<model>/AGENTS.md`. Global instructions move to `~/.lunr/agent/agents/AGENTS.md`. - `settings_load` exposes four narrow settings tools on demand. - Enabled model tier

#42 feat: add tier-routed subagents and model-specific instructions M ## Summary - require every child execution to select a configured light, standard, or heavy route, preserve chain/parallel execution, and fail closed instead of inheriting the parent model - make subagent elapsed time update in whole seconds and use `ran for` on terminal rows, while keeping the existing aggregate-launch safety behind a default-on setting - add global/model-specific AGENTS.md instructions with safe provider-independent 

#30 feat: finish prompt-driven subagent cutover M Supersedes #28 after #26 and #27 landed. ## Summary - replace named-agent discovery with generic `{ task, description, permissions? }` children - complete the foreground and async `ChildSpec` cutover - remove builtin agent markdown, CRUD/profile/saved-chain surfaces, and legacy named-agent modules - keep private child IDs separate from description-first UI labels - fix scheduled singles, appended/dynamic child ID collisions, and

#28 feat: generic prompt-driven subagents U ## Summary Replace predefined subagent types with generic, model-prompted children. Each child is `{ task, description, permissions? }`: - `description` is required UI metadata (single-line, max 80) - `permissions` is `full` or `read-only`; omitted means full - Full is child-safe coding tools (read/search/shell/edit/write/web/LSP/MCP), excluding cron/memory/behavior/goals/plan-approval/nested subagents - Plan parents may launch only 

#24 fix: normalize swarm approve for 0.2.11 publish M Unblocks `v0.2.11` npm publish. `ApprovalResponse.approve` is not an `ApprovalDecision`; cache it as `once` so sibling SINGLE calls share the allow.

#23 release: v0.2.11 same-turn swarm, gateway /new, cron allowlist M ## Summary - Same-turn SINGLE `subagent` calls count toward the swarm gate. One once/reject covers that assistant message. Same-turn singles overlap; sequential work stays `chain`. - Gateway `/new` while busy aborts the live turn and drops the queue. - TUI cron uses the same deliver allowlist as the gateway. Delivery also refuses a persisted chat that is not home/allowed/origin. - Corrupt models-store JSON is treated as empty. - Plan-mo

#2 feat(agent): agent-swarm approval gate for auto-activated parallel fan-out U ## What An auto-activated agent swarm — one `subagent` tool call launching **more than 2 parallel subagents** — now requires user approval in **manual and yolo** modes. Only `auto` mode bypasses the gate. Explicit `/swarm` turns are pre-approved (the user already asked for the swarm). TUI dialog: ``` ▶ Approve AgentSwarm? agent swarm (4 subagents) Explore lunR auth/model/settings/plan systems 1. Approve once 2. Approve for this

text:
---
name: code-review
description: "Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to \"review since X\"."
---

Two-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:

- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?
- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?

Both axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.

The issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.

## Process

### 1. Pin the fixed point

Whatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.

Capture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.

Before going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.

### 2. Identify the spec source

Look for the originating spec, in this order:

1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.
2. A path the user passed as an argument.
3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.
4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report "no spec available".

### 3. Identify the standards sources

Anything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

On top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:

- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.
- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic ("possible Feature Envy"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.

Each smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:

- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.
- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.
- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.
- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.
- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.
- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.
- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.
- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.
- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.
- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.
- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.
- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.

### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel

**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:

- The full diff command and commit list.
- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).
- The brief: "Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words."

**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:

- The diff command and commit list.
- The path or fetched contents of the spec.
- The brief: "Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words."

If the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.

### 5. Aggregate

Present the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).

End with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.

## Why two axes

A change can pass one axis and fail the other:

- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**
- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**

Reporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.

---
name: diagnosing-bugs
description: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.
---

# Diagnosing Bugs

A discipline for hard bugs. Skip phases only when explicitly justified.

When exploring the codebase, read `CONTEXT.md` (if it exists) to get a clear mental model of the relevant modules, and check ADRs in the area you're touching.

## Redact

This skill has you show commands, outputs and captured artifacts. **Redact every secret first**: write `<REDACTED>` in its place. Build loops against env vars, so the credential stays in the environment rather than in what you show. Captured artifacts carry auth headers: quote only the lines that carry the signal.

If the redacted output is not enough to diagnose the bug, say so and ask the user.

## Phase 1: Build a feedback loop

**This is the skill.** Everything else is mechanical. If you have a **tight** pass/fail signal for the bug (one that goes red on _this_ bug), you will find the cause; bisection, hypothesis-testing, and instrumentation all just consume it. If you don't have one, no amount of staring at code will save you.

Spend disproportionate effort here. **Be aggressive. Be creative. Refuse to give up.**

### Ways to construct one, in roughly this order

1. **Failing test** at whatever seam reaches the bug: unit, integration, e2e.
2. **Curl / HTTP script** against a running dev server.
3. **CLI invocation** with a fixture input, diffing stdout against a known-good snapshot.
4. **Headless browser script** (Playwright / Puppeteer) that drives the UI and asserts on DOM/console/network.
5. **Replay a captured trace.** Save a real network request / payload / event log to disk; replay it through the code path in isolation.
6. **Throwaway harness.** Spin up a minimal subset of the system (one service, mocked deps) that exercises the bug code path with a single function call.
7. **Property / fuzz loop.** If the bug is "sometimes wrong output", run 1000 random inputs and look for the failure mode.
8. **Bisection harness.** If the bug appeared between two known states (commit, dataset, version), automate "boot at state X, check, repeat" so you can `git bisect run` it.
9. **Differential loop.** Run the same input through old-version vs new-version (or two configs) and diff outputs.
10. **HITL bash script.** Last resort. If a human must click, drive _them_ with `scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh` so the loop is still structured. Captured output feeds back to you.

Build the right feedback loop, and the bug is 90% fixed.

### Tighten the loop

Treat the loop as a product. Once you have _a_ loop, **tighten** it:

- Can I make it faster? (Cache setup, skip unrelated init, narrow the test scope.)
- Can I make the signal sharper? (Assert on the specific symptom, not "didn't crash".)
- Can I make it more deterministic? (Pin time, seed RNG, isolate filesystem, freeze network.)

A 30-second flaky loop is barely better than no loop; a 2-second deterministic one is tight, a debugging superpower.

### Non-deterministic bugs

The goal is not a clean repro but a **higher reproduction rate**. Loop the trigger 100×, parallelise, add stress, narrow timing windows, inject sleeps. A 50%-flake bug is debuggable; 1% is not, so keep raising the rate until it's debuggable.

### When you genuinely cannot build a loop

Stop and say so explicitly. List what you tried. Ask the user for: (a) access to whatever environment reproduces it, (b) a redacted captured artifact (HAR file, log dump, core dump, screen recording with timestamps), or (c) permission to add temporary production instrumentation. Do **not** proceed to hypothesise without a loop.

### Completion criterion: a tight loop that goes red

Phase 1 is done when the loop is **tight** and **red-capable**: you can name **one command** (a script path, a test invocation, a curl) that you have **already run at least once** (show the invocation and its output, redacted), and that is:

- [ ] **Red-capable**: it drives the actual bug code path and asserts the **user's exact symptom**, so it can go red on this bug and green once fixed. Not "runs without erroring"; it must be able to _catch this specific bug_.

## Subagent audit at `b57c148`

I reviewed source and assertions for subagent launch, child permissions, async continuation, supervisor questions, intercom, watchdog startup, and approvals. With inherited subagent and intercom environment variables removed, **292 focused tests passed across 23 suites**. No product files, tests, or staged files changed.

### Findings

- **High: read-only mode permits executable shell commands.** `packages/coding-agent/src/core/plan-mode.ts:117-143,150-160,361-369` blocks a short list of package-manager subcommands and matches Node execution flags only as exact strings. In read-only mode, source-level calls to `gateToolCall("bash", …)` allowed `node --eval=0`, `npm run build`, `pnpm run build`, `yarn run build`, and `npm exec -- echo ok`. These were classified as strings; I did **not** execute the commands. The source calls its Bash heuristic “not a security boundary,” but these allowed forms can run code that writes files.
- **Medium: explicit async singles bypass the large-launch confirmation.** `packages/coding-agent/src/core/large-subagent-launch.ts:13-15,33-35,48-61` excludes `async:true` siblings from the count. A source-level reproduction with three same-turn read-only child calls returned `count:0`, three allowed gate results, and `prompts:0` despite a registered reject handler. This differs from omitted `async`, which now launches asynchronously by default and is counted. No children were spawned in the reproduction.

The existing tests cover ordinary sibling counting and read-only Bash cases, but not those two inputs.

### Coverage and limits

The qualified subagent work represented by #23, #24, #25, #30, #38, #47, #51, #57, #62, #66, #72, and #86 was checked against current source and focused tests. Later qualified release integrations #97, #104, and #112 were assessed as current-tree integration coverage, not as independent live releases. The remaining requested PRs primarily concern subsystems assigned to other reviewers. In the supplied PR dataset, unmerged #2's swarm proposal is superseded by the #23/#24 gate, #28 by #30's completed child cutover, and #61 by #62's schema fix.

An earlier run in the **wrong, dirty checkout** failed one supervisor-continuation test because inherited `PI_SUBAGENT_*` variables routed its fixture request toward the real parent. I notified the parent to ignore that request. The same test passed in the corrected clean worktree with those variables removed; it is not a clean-worktree baseline failure.

Separate pi-remnant note: these modules retain compatible `PI_SUBAGENT_*` and `PI_INTERCOM_*` environment names, `@earendil-works/pi-*` imports, and the `pi-intercom` protocol/pipe name. The `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` reference at `pi-subagents/src/runs/shared/model-fallback.ts:177` is a stale explanatory comment, not an observed runtime write. I found no executable `~/.pi/` path in the inspected subagent/intercom modules. No live provider, installed CLI, daily-driver dist, or published package was tested; junctioned dependencies mean these results do not validate a fresh compiled artifact.
